question: Does NKE's multi-timeframe price, moving-average, and volume tape signal base accumulation or an active Stage 4 markdown?

epigraph.quote: An oversold oscillator inside a falling 30-week structure measures velocity, not a durable floor.

web_blocks.html: Both our quantitative facts ledger and live TradingView snapshot place NKE in Stage 4 (Markdown) as of November 20, 2026 [42]. The official facts ledger closes at $32.92 (-4.11% 1D, -13.35% 1W, -19.21% 3M). TradingView's snapshot and options package record $32.94 (-4.06% 1D, -13.10% 1W), a $0.02 (0.06%) tick variance [42, 44]. Meanwhile, the broader U.S. market sits in a Downtrend with 10 distribution days in 25 sessions. Only 38.8% of tracked stocks sit above their 50-day SMA, and zero of nine S&P sectors hold their 20-day SMA.

Weekly and daily snapshots confirm sustained institutional distribution rather than Stage 1 basing [42]. On the weekly chart (1W), NKE trades 18.42% below a falling 30-week SMA ($40.38) and 10.76% below its 10-week EMA ($36.91), with weekly RSI at 31.06 [42]. On the daily chart (1D), every major moving average slopes downward overhead: 10-day SMA at $37.03, 20-day SMA at $37.81, 50-day SMA at $36.69, and 200-day SMA at $44.12, while daily RSI sits at 31.66 (facts) / 31.70 (TradingView) [42].

Our NKE multi-timeframe options snapshot (options_US_batch3.json) adds intraday 4-hour (4H) context for the November 20 close [44]. On the 4H chart, post-Investor-Day selling pushed 4H RSI to 24.91 below the 4H 20-EMA ($36.45) and 4H 50-SMA ($37.84), widening Bollinger Band width to 21.4% [44]. Oversold intraday readings can spark sharp bounces toward Pivot S1 ($34.02) or the 50-day SMA ($36.69). Even so, trading below the 50D SMA ($36.69), 30W SMA ($40.38), and 200D SMA ($44.12) earns NO OPTIONS EDGE for long calls or LEAPS [44].

web_blocks.title: Why Scanner Support Levels Differ from Actionable Support

web_blocks.html: The automated technical screen table above carries one important nuance. Its formula anchors support around the 50-day SMA ($36.14–$37.24, stop $35.91) [42]. Because NKE already broke lower to $32.92, that band now sits 10%–13% above price as overhead supply. Meanwhile, our November 13 review anchored a structural stop at $31.50, right below the $31.97 52-week low.

Catching a Stage 4 falling knife inside a 10-distribution-day Downtrend violates capital preservation. We also face Q2 FY2027 earnings on December 17, 2026 ($0.38 consensus EPS) [24, 43]. To heal technically, NKE must first stop making lower lows below $31.97. It then needs a multi-month Stage 1 base followed by a high-volume reclaim of the 50-day SMA ($36.69) and 30-week SMA ($40.38).

book_paragraphs: Price action confirms what the November 17 Investor Day guidance implied: NKE has entered a decisive Weinstein Stage 4 markdown inside a U.S. Downtrend. On November 20, 2026, the official market-facts ledger closed at $32.92, down 4.11% on the day and 13.35% for the week. TradingView's snapshot closed at $32.94, a two-cent tick difference. Across the S&P 500, ten distribution days in twenty-five sessions have pushed market breadth below 39% above the 50-day average, while zero of nine sectors hold their 20-day average.

Weekly and daily charts confirm active institutional selling. Weekly price sits 18.42% below a falling 30-week average ($40.38) and 10.76% below the 10-week EMA ($36.91), with weekly RSI at 31.06. Daily price sits beneath downward-sloping 10-day ($37.03), 20-day ($37.81), 50-day ($36.69), and 200-day ($44.12) averages, with daily RSI near 31.7. Friday's selloff hit 32.0 million shares, or 1.33 times the 20-day average, confirming real institutional supply.

In the NKE multi-timeframe options snapshot (options_US_batch3), four-hour RSI dropped to 24.91 below the 4H 20-EMA ($36.45) and 4H 50-SMA ($37.84), with Bollinger Band width stretched to 21.4%. Oversold intraday levels often trigger brief bounces toward Pivot S1 ($34.02) or the broken 50-day average ($36.69). Yet bounces inside Stage 4 act as exits, not durable floors. Accordingly, the options overlay assigns NO OPTIONS EDGE and rejects both long calls and LEAPS.

Automated screens still list theoretical support at $36.14 to $37.24 around the 50-day average. Because NKE already sliced 10.2% below that level, that zone has flipped into overhead supply. Shares now hover just $0.95 above the $31.97 52-week low and $1.42 above our prior $31.50 stop, with 7.91% of the float (92.92 million shares) sold short and Pivot S2 sitting lower at $29.36.

Three technical repairs must occur before NKE earns fresh capital. First, shares must hold above $31.97 through December 17 Q2 earnings ($0.38 consensus). Second, price must build a tight Stage 1 horizontal base as the 50-day average flattens. Third, NKE must reclaim both the 50-day and 30-week averages on strong accumulation volume while 63-day relative strength (-9.51%) turns positive.

Price action across weekly, daily, and intraday horizons leaves zero ambiguity about institutional supply dominance. On November 20, 2026, NIKE fell 4.11 percent to $32.92 on 32.00 million shares, sitting 1.33 times its twenty-day average volume and closing only $0.95 above the $31.97 fifty-two-week low. All primary moving averages slope steadily lower overhead, led by the 50-day simple moving average at $36.69, the 10-week exponential average at $36.91, the 30-week average at $40.38, and the 200-day average at $44.12.

Attempting to buy an oversold Stage 4 decline inside a broad S&P 500 Downtrend with ten distribution days ignores the basic mechanics of capital preservation. Overhead volume shelves between $36.14 and $37.24 will attract trapped sellers on any reflex rally into the December 17 quarterly report. Options pricing reflects that fragility as well, delivering no favorable call-spread asymmetry while implied volatility remains elevated into a low-visibility earnings reset.
